title: File layout: partition a Delta table so queries can skip files
objective_text: Choose a partition column that matches how a table is read and has few distinct values, and write the Delta table with it.
scenario: Finance reads sales one month at a time, and the table will hold years of data. The first version was written as one undivided table. Write it so a month's query can skip every other month's files, without making thousands of tiny folders.
engine_label: Python with delta-rs and Polars on this PC
verifies: Your script ran on this PC and wrote a Delta table partitioned by sale_month, one partition per month, with all 600 sales once each.
does_not_verify: How Spark in Fabric prunes partitions or uses file statistics when it reads: this checks the table's layout in its log, not a query plan.
Whether partitioning is worth it at your real data size: small tables often read faster unpartitioned.

hints: A good partition column matches the filter readers use and has few distinct values. How do reports filter this table?
Partitioning by sale_date makes one folder per day; by sale_id, one per sale. Both make many tiny files.
Add sale_month with pl.col('sale_date').dt.strftime('%Y-%m'), then write_deltalake(TABLE, ..., partition_by=['sale_month']).
explanation: Partitioning writes each value of a column to its own folder, so a query filtering on that column reads only the matching folders. It helps only when queries filter on the column and each partition holds plenty of data: a high-cardinality column (a date at day level for a small table, or an id) produces many tiny files and slows everything down. A month column suits monthly reporting. For finer pruning inside partitions, Delta also keeps per-file statistics, and Fabric can apply V-Order when it writes or optimizes.
